result.judge_notes: pass 1 (A=without, B=with): Both pages list only the outstanding invoices, sort them most overdue first, label the status in words and show the $750.00 still owed on #1044. B states the currency once in its column headers, shows the invoice total, amount paid and balance in separate right-aligned columns, adds a totals row and puts icons on the status badges. A's choice to put the issue date and invoice total in small text under the customer name makes those figures harder to scan. B leaves the issue date out entirely, which costs it a little on item 5. | pass 2 (A=with, B=without): Both pages list only unpaid invoices, sorted with the most overdue first, and both show the correct $750.00 balance for the part-paid invoice. A goes further: it has separate Invoice total, Paid and Balance columns with right-aligned figures and the currency stated once in the headers, it adds icons to the status badges, and it ends with a totals row. B tucks the issue dates and totals into the customer subtext instead of giving them their own columns, and its badges rely on text and color only.
